steps.title: Keep one row per employee
steps.change: The question asks for every employee, including employees receiving zero. Read Employees and keep all five rows. Apply the conditions inside the bonus calculation.
steps.added_sql: SELECT employee_id, name, salary FROM Employees ORDER BY employee_id;
steps.sql: SELECT employee_id, name, salary FROM Employees ORDER BY employee_id;

steps.title: Check the two requirements for each employee
steps.change: An odd ID has remainder 1 when divided by 2. The name test excludes names starting with M. AND requires both checks to pass.
steps.added_sql:
SELECT employee_id, name, salary,
       employee_id % 2 AS remainder,
       name NOT LIKE 'M%' AS name_allowed
FROM Employees ORDER BY employee_id;
steps.sql:
SELECT employee_id, name, salary,
       employee_id % 2 AS remainder,
       name NOT LIKE 'M%' AS name_allowed
FROM Employees ORDER BY employee_id;

steps.title: Choose the bonus and order the result
steps.change: CASE returns salary when both checks are true, and ELSE returns zero for everyone else. Select employee_id and bonus, and order by employee_id ascending.
steps.added_sql:
SELECT employee_id,
       CASE
           WHEN name NOT LIKE 'M%' AND employee_id % 2 = 1 THEN salary
           ELSE 0
       END AS bonus
FROM Employees
ORDER BY employee_id ASC;
